name: Jabil
description: Jabil builds other companies' products. Customers such as cloud providers, carmakers, medical-device makers and consumer-electronics brands hire Jabil to design, build and ship their products from factories in places such as China, Malaysia, Mexico and the US. As a turnkey manufacturer Jabil is responsible for buying the components, which is why cost of revenue is about 91 percent of sales (nine months FY2026, computed) and segment income was only 5.4 percent of FY2025 revenue ($1.62B on $29.8B). Revenue is concentrated: five customers are about 36 percent and one (Customer A) is 16 percent. The mix has shifted toward AI data-center equipment (Intelligent Infrastructure was 41 percent of FY2025 revenue, up from 32 percent) while the consumer Mobility business was divested.

businessLines.name: Regulated Industries (reportable segment)
businessLines.how: Customers in regulated markets pay Jabil per finished product or assembly for engineering, manufacturing and supply chain; Jabil buys the components (turnkey) so revenue includes material cost.
businessLines.description: Customers primarily in automotive and transportation, healthcare and packaging, and renewables and energy infrastructure.

businessLines.name: Intelligent Infrastructure (reportable segment)
businessLines.how: Cloud, data center and networking customers pay Jabil per system built (Customer A, 16% of company revenue, is reported mainly here); as a turnkey manufacturer Jabil buys the components, so revenue is large relative to segment income. FY2025 revenue +34% came mainly from a 30% rise from existing cloud and data center customers.
businessLines.description: Customers primarily in capital equipment, cloud and data center infrastructure, and networking and communications (including AI infrastructure).

businessLines.name: Connected Living and Digital Commerce (reportable segment)
businessLines.how: Customers pay Jabil per unit built or per automation system delivered; revenue fell 25% in FY2025 mainly because the Mobility business was divested, while digital commerce revenue grew 2%.
businessLines.description: Customers primarily in connected living (consumer devices) and digital commerce (warehouse automation and robotics).

brands.name: Mobility business (divested)
brands.note: Divested in FY2025; the 10-K cites BYDE in an indemnification note tied to the closing. Drove the 27% drop in connected living revenue. Sale date and price not extracted.
